This man was from Thrace, from the village of Bederiana;
he was an old and simple man.
And because the Thracians, his countrymen, mocked him [saying]:
"If you accept the Synod of Chalcedon, which was convened through the zeal of Leo of Rome,
all the regions of Italy will be at peace with him,
and there will be one kingdom,"
he accepted it.
And when Qubad {OCR: ܘܟܲܕ݂ ܩܵܡ̣ -> ܩܘܿܒ݂ܵܕ݂?}, king of the Persians, arose,
he demanded from Justin, king of the Romans, five hundred and fifty hundredweights (centenaria) of gold,
those which used to be given to him for the expenses of the Persian garrison who guarded the Gates of the Caspian against the Huns;
and he would not give [it].
From time to time he would send his Arabs into the land of the Romans,
and they raided and took captives.
Therefore, Mundhir, king of the Arabs, went up and took captive the entire region of the limes, that is, the borders:
Balikh and Khabur.
And they also crossed into Arzan and Nisibis,
and took captives, plundered, and slaughtered {OCR: ܩܲܛܸܓܼܘ -> ܩܲܛܸܠܘ}.
And he went up again to Homs, and also to Apamea, and to the region of Antioch,
and he killed, took captives, and devastated;
and he selected from the captives four hundred virgins.
At this time there appeared in the region of Cilicia a woman who did not speak;
and she was taller by a cubit than all men,
and no one knew where she was from.
Moreover, she ate food like human beings,
and from every shop she would take one obol (follis).
And suddenly she was not seen again.
Now that old Justin, at the end of his days, set up with him Justinian, his sister's son,
and proclaimed him Caesar.
And after three months, he, the old man, died.
After Justin the old man, Justinian, his sister's son, [ruled] thirty-eight years.
At the beginning of his reign he went down toward the Persians and came to Mabbugh.
And when he was told about Theodora, the daughter of a certain Orthodox priest,
he sought her [in marriage].
Her father, however, was not willing to give his daughter
until he made a covenant that he would not compel her to accept the Synod of Chalcedon.
This [emperor] sent Belisarius to wage war with the Persians.
And when the week of the salvific Passion was at hand,
the commander of the Persians sent to him, saying:
"Let us honor the festival for the sake of the Nazarenes and Jews who are with me,
and for your sake, O Christians."
